why: Tree DP meets knapsack: choosing a node requires its parent, so in preorder each node is either taken (continue into its subtree) or skipped (its whole subtree is skipped). dp[i][c] over preorder positions gives an O(n * capacity) tree knapsack.
hints: A valid selection is a connected set containing the root. What does skipping a node forbid?
List nodes in preorder; a subtree is a contiguous range [i, i + size). At position i: take node i and move to i+1 with budget c - cost, or skip and jump to i + size.
dp[i][c] = max(dp[i + size][c], value + dp[i+1][c - cost]) filled from the end of the preorder; answer dp[0][capacity]. (Merging child knapsacks also works, in O(n * capacity^2).)
pitfalls: Selecting nothing is allowed: the answer is at least 0 even if the root is unaffordable.
Compute subtree sizes iteratively; recursion can be 200 deep, which is fine, but be careful in general.
